claims.text: The baseline is a FeNiCrCoCu thin coating on a conventional metal substrate with no tungsten addition.
The controlled intervention is a fixed low tungsten addition while keeping all other deposition parameters identical.
Adding tungsten to FeNiCrCoCu increases lattice distortion.
Tungsten atoms are larger than the constituent atoms of the FeNiCrCoCu matrix, and this size difference causes lattice distortion.
Tungsten-induced lattice distortion pins dislocations in the coating.
Tungsten addition produces a higher density of pinned dislocations.
Tungsten addition refines the coating microstructure and produces finer grains.
Tungsten-induced distortion and dislocation pinning stabilize grain boundaries during high-temperature sliding.
The tungsten-modified microstructure limits localized microscopic plastic deformation during sliding.
Tungsten addition increases the hardness of the coating.
The increase in hardness caused by the tungsten-modified microstructure reduces wear.
The tungsten-doped FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a lower wear rate than the tungsten-free coating during high-temperature sliding.
The tungsten-doped coating will have a lower or stabilized friction coefficient during high-temperature sliding.
Oxidation and dynamic-strain effects become significant at approximately 600–800 °C.
The predicted wear and deformation effects should hold during sliding at approximately 600–800 °C under the tested load and speed.
At sufficiently high tungsten concentrations, the beneficial effect may saturate or tungsten may cause embrittlement.
The optimum tungsten concentration and magnitude of wear improvement depend on processing and test parameters.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits a merely stabilized friction coefficient, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant friction reduction; an unchanged but stable coefficient could therefore both satisfy the prediction and trigger falsification.
